subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: Should OpenClaw add a core global agent dry-run mode, and which execution surfaces must be covered before users can trust it as a safety boundary?
rationale: This adds a new CLI flag and safety semantics across tool execution paths; automation cannot choose whether adapter-only interception is acceptable or whether Gateway, client-hosted, CLI-backend, and provider-native tools must be included from day one.

options.title: Design the core safety contract first
options.body: Specify the supported surfaces and preview/result shape, then implement only the covered mode with tests proving no side effects through those paths.

options.title: Fold into broader safe modes
options.body: Track this under the wider ask/plan/modify product direction and keep this issue as a focused requirement for tool-call preview semantics.

options.title: Decline global interception
options.body: Keep per-command dry-runs and plugin policy hooks as the supported safety tools, and close this direction after a maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Design the core safety contract first
recommendation.body: Specify the supported surfaces and preview/result shape, then implement only the covered mode with tests proving no side effects through those paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is on the current agent CLI and adapter surfaces that would anchor the design.
